ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, point $M$ is on the side $BC$ of the equilateral triangle $\triangle ABC$, with $BM = 8$. The ray $CD$ is perpendicular to $BC$ at point $C$. Point $P$ is a moving point on ray $CD$, and point $N$ is a moving point on line segment $AB$. When the value of $MP+NP$ is minimized, $BN = 9$. What is the length of $AC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle, \\
thus $AC=BC$ and $\angle B=60^\circ$, \\
Let point $M$ be the symmetric point with respect to line $CD$ and construct $GN\perp AB$ at $N$ intersecting $CD$ at $P$, \\
then, at this time, the value of $MP+PN$ is minimized, \\
Since $\angle B=60^\circ$ and $\angle BNG=90^\circ$, \\
thus $\angle G=30^\circ$, \\
Since $BN=9$, \\
thus $BG=2BN=18$, \\
thus $MG=BG-BM=18-8=10$, \\
thus $CM=CG=5$, \\
thus $AC=BC=\boxed{13}$.

method.method_draft: Geometric unfolding/reflection method. From the image, read that B, M, C lie on the horizontal base in that order, CD is the vertical ray through C, P lies on CD, N lies on AB, and the broken path is M-P-N. From the text, use that triangle ABC is equilateral, BM=8, and at the minimum BN=9. Reflect M across the vertical line CD to a point G on the extension of BC to the right of C. For any P on CD, MP=GP, so minimizing MP+PN is equivalent to minimizing GP+PN. The shortest path from G to AB crossing CD is the straight segment from G to N, and since N is free on AB, the minimizing N is the perpendicular foot from G to AB. Thus GN is perpendicular to AB. In right triangle BNG, angle B is 60 degrees, so it is a 30-60-90 triangle and BG=2*BN=18. Since BM=8, MG=BG-BM=10. Because G is the reflection of M across CD, C is the midpoint of MG, so CM=CG=5. Therefore BC=BM+MC=8+5=13, and since the triangle is equilateral, AC=13.

method.method_draft: Coordinate/first-order minimization method. From the image, set B=(0,0), take BC as the x-axis, and let C=(s,0), where s=AC=BC is the unknown side length. Then A=(s/2, sqrt(3)s/2), M=(8,0), CD is the vertical line x=s, P=(s,y), and a point N on AB with BN=u has coordinates N=(u/2, sqrt(3)u/2). From the text, at the minimum u=BN=9. Minimize F(u,y)=MP+NP. At an interior minimum, varying N along AB gives NP perpendicular to AB, so the vector from N to P is perpendicular to direction (1/2, sqrt(3)/2). This gives y=(2u-s)/sqrt(3). Varying P along the vertical line CD gives cancellation of vertical components of the two unit direction vectors; using the perpendicular condition for NP, this simplifies to y/sqrt((s-8)^2+y^2)=1/2, hence s-8=sqrt(3)y. Substitute y=(2u-s)/sqrt(3) and u=9: s-8=18-s, so s=13. Therefore AC=13.

先描述图像：图中是一个顶点A在上、B在左下、C在右下的三角形，题意说明它是等边三角形；点M在底边BC上，且BM=8。过C作向上的垂线射线CD，点P在这条竖直射线上；点N在边AB上。图中还画出了从N到P、从M到P的连线，用来表示长度MP+NP。
推理：设B=(0,0)，C=(s,0)，则等边三角形ABC中A=(s/2, √3 s/2)，其中s=AC=BC。因为BM=8，所以M=(8,0)。设BN=u，则N在AB上可表示为N=(u/2, √3 u/2)。把M关于直线CD（即x=s）对称到M'=(2s-8,0)。对固定的N，MP+NP在P∈CD上最小时，折线M-P-N可反射为直线M'-N，因此P是直线M'N与CD的交点；再对N作最小化时，M'N必须垂直于AB。这就是一阶最优条件。
AB的方向向量可取(1/2, √3/2)，所以与AB垂直的直线斜率为-1/√3。于是M'与N连线的斜率满足
(√3 u / 2) / (u/2 - (2s-8)) = -1/√3。
化简得 3u/2 = -u/2 + 2s - 8，进而 2u = 2s - 8，故 s = u + 4。题目给出最优时BN=u=9，所以 s=13。
因此 AC=BC=13。

(√3 u / 2) / (u/2 - (2s-8)) = -1/√3。
化简得 3u/2 = -u/2 + 2s - 8，进而 2u = 2s - 8，故 s = u + 4。题目给出最优时BN=u=9，所以 s=13。
因此 AC=BC=13。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, point $M$ is on side $BC$ of the equilateral triangle $\triangle ABC$, with $BM=8$. Ray $CD$ is perpendicular to $BC$ at point $C$. Point $P$ is a moving point on ray $CD$, and point $N$ is a moving point on segment $AB$. When the value of $MP+NP$ is minimized, $BN=9$. What is the length of $AC$?
raw_record.answer: Solution: Since $\triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle, $AC=BC$ and $\angle B=60^\circ$. Let point $M$ be the symmetric point with respect to line $CD$, and construct $GN\perp AB$ at $N$, intersecting $CD$ at $P$. Then at this time, the value of $MP+PN$ is minimized. Since $\angle B=60^\circ$ and $\angle BNG=90^\circ$, $\angle G=30^\circ$. Since $BN=9$, $BG=2BN=18$, thus $MG=BG-BM=18-8=10$, thus $CM=CG=5$, thus $AC=BC=\boxed{13}$.

Image description: In the figure, the base BC of triangle ABC is horizontal, point B is at the lower left, point C is at the lower right, and point A is above, forming the shape of an equilateral triangle. Point M is located on BC and between B and C. Draw vertical ray CD through C, CD is perpendicular to BC, and point D is above C. Point P is on vertical ray CD, point N is on side AB, and the broken-line path in the figure is M-P-N.

Reasoning: Because △ABC is an equilateral triangle, ∠B=60°, and AC=BC. To minimize MP+NP, reflect point M about line CD to point G; then G is on the right-side extension of BC, and for any P on CD, MP=GP. Therefore minimizing MP+PN is equivalent to minimizing GP+PN. The shortest path should be the straight line segment from G to AB, and since N can move on AB, at the minimum GN is perpendicular to AB. Thus in △BNG, ∠BNG=90°, ∠B=60°, so ∠G=30°, and △BNG is a 30°-60°-90° triangle. It is known that at the minimum BN=9, therefore the hypotenuse BG=2BN=18. Also BM=8, and B, M, C, G are collinear, so MG=BG-BM=18-8=10. Since G is the symmetric point of M about CD, C is the midpoint of MG, therefore CM=CG=5. Thus BC=BM+MC=8+5=13. In an equilateral triangle AC=BC, so AC=13.
